title: Prove the exact one-step Schur commutator criterion
body:
## Summary

A scoped algebraic proof gives the exact commutator after deleting a common admitted scalar pivot from two commuting matrices over any field:

```text
P = [[p,r],[c,D]], Q = [[q,s],[e,F]], PQ = QP = [[h,t],[w,J]], p,q != 0
S = D-c r/p, T = F-e s/q
u = c/p-e/q, v = r/p-s/q, x = w-h e/q, y = t-h s/q
[S,T] = x v-u y
```

This gives a necessary-and-sufficient zero criterion and a complete rank-0/1/2 trichotomy. The rank-two bound is sharp even for two commuting rank-two idempotents in dimension three over F5. It answers the one-step commutativity part of #4259 open question 1; it does not classify the full Schur-pair orbit or count complete headers. No new κ or supplier admission.

Only `research/schur-commutator-criterion/` is added. The side theorem changes the scope of the `uniform-transfer-audit` card to original successor work. The proof is self-contained; predecessor results are cited context, not audit deliverables. This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas.

## Evidence

Before, the laminar preservation proof left a nonnested pair's changing Schur state unspecified. After, the explicit vector factorization decides commutativity and its rank defect at that boundary.

- Every admitted commuting pair in five small domains is checked directly: 1,864 arbitrary F2 matrices at m=3; 420 arbitrary F3 pairs at m=2; 253 F2 idempotent pairs at m=3; 2,572 F3 idempotent pairs at m=3; 76 F5 idempotent pairs at m=2. The overlapping domains are not claimed as disjoint counts.
- All 20,160 GL4(F2) headers for one overlapping coordinate pair are enumerated. Both pivots pass in 5,040 headers; 3,696 leave commuting complements and 1,344 give rank-one commutators. These are header counts, not distinct-pair counts.
- A new explicit F5 projector pair attains commutator rank two. All 7,442 declared vector quadruples check the degenerate zero criterion, and four controls detect false preservation, wrong sign, omitted product-pivot correction and missing input commutation.
- Both registered commands pass locally on CPython 3.12.15, macOS 27.0.1 arm64. Final directly timed normal and optimized checks took 1.31 s and 1.27 s, below their 120 s limits. These are check durations, not performance comparisons.
- Package metadata, five-file committed-byte/source-history preflight, official committed export and export integrity pass. Both read-only Git-free modes reproduce exactly the committed normal/optimized receipt, including all five source hashes. Receipt SHA256: `fe80df2a5e858cfb377490b2acd739959c25771231ddfa60966e078b08ef15d7`.

Reproduce from the repository root, using CPython 3.12. Another CPython 3.12 path may replace this local interpreter:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/schur-commutator-criterion/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -O -B research/schur-commutator-criterion/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/schur-commutator-criterion
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/schur-commutator-criterion --check-source-history
```

Expected markers are `PASS_SCHUR_COMMUTATOR_CRITERION`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=completed` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`. No pending predecessor executable, external live input or third-party Python package is needed. The source pins bind historical provenance.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The universal claim is the written field-algebra proof, with finite corroboration. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. This covers one scalar deletion with two nonzero pivots. Noncommuting inputs, nonfield rings, block pivots, later-step orbit distributions and complete header-count laws remain outside scope. Header selection/emission, an actual producer, dispatch, dirty return, stock and the complete caller bill remain unpriced. No selected cold replay, Lean/Docker build or complete multiplication theorem is supplied.

All registered local checks ran. Ruff is unavailable, so no external static analyzer was run; Python warnings-as-errors and AST syntax/function-size inspection were used. Bounded dynamic allocations and the code constraints are documented in the README.

## Open next questions

1. Classify simultaneous Schur-pair orbits and transition weights for nonnested commuting projectors. Start with the two rank-two requests in dimension three; the commutator rank alone does not identify the full orbit. Coordinate with the active corank-one counting work.
2. Extend the factorization to a common invertible block pivot and find its sharp commutator-rank bound. The scalar rearrangements used here do not transfer directly.

## Related open work

- #4259, head `2a582d8f66d1900b22ee2cd0062ee5dca94e8f85`: immediate structural predecessor and open question. This adds the exact one-step commutator beyond laminar preservation. No header fraction is computed or numerically compared here.
- #4261, head `4728fc766b3084f3ab2f5c8543a5e74e4a12b126`: counts overlapping corank-one full guards without classifying Schur pairs. This supplies a structural criterion, with no overlapping aggregate number to compare.
- #4273, head `53c2d5a3a43c0538c3d8c263bdb65c29e330b068`: ternary corank-one counting formula. Different output quantity; no joint fraction is asserted here.
- #4274, head `497b8862d98ab57e33b262fa2631afc5a559257f`: initially noncommuting one-way corank-one requests. Its input premise differs; no shared aggregate number is claimed.
- #4275, head `a3ba3670815329ac69c84c0ea0fefcfa16d7cbff`: gives the exact joint full-guard fraction over every finite field for k corank-one requests with pairwise orthogonal rank-one kernels. It counts complete passing headers; this package decides whether one Schur deletion preserves a commuting pair. No header fraction is computed here, so no overlapping numerical result is claimed.
- #4228, head `bb25dcedb5bbbacd3c35359eb6b5488b087bcde6`: existing single-request Schur/rank framework and densities. The sharp F5 example has input ranks 2 and Schur ranks 1, agreeing numerically with its rank-drop lemma. No marginal density is computed here.
- #4240, head `9f9c89ed75e9fdae6b6762925b080fb308824858`: classifies nonorthogonal rank-one header counts. This treats the Schur commutator of a previously commuting pair, without a shared count to compare.
- #4246 / #4239: orthogonal full-chain and rank-one laws. Those preserved subclasses are context; this adds the defect criterion outside them, with no new guard fraction or overlapping aggregate number.
- #4227: extreme-rank marginal laws, a different quantity; no shared marginal count is claimed.
- #4100, head `337d04939571a637aeab54a0f58f54fde811663a`: Cinna Davis's BIT request/complete-header context. No physical invoice or multiplication claim is compared or admitted.
- #4209: Schur majorant closure for a parity-triangular complex caller, a different matrix contract and quantity. No shared numerical result.

The preceding header packages are by Nick Petalas. Cinna Davis supplies the BIT request context. No predecessor source or credit line is changed. The live three-kernel counting claim is a separate question.
